Add a dynamical ecosystem component

Source: R/extension.R
setComponent.Rd

By default, mizer models any number of size-resolved consumer species and a single size-resolved resource spectrum. Your model may require additional components, like for example detritus or carrion or multiple resources or .... This function allows you to set up such components.

Usage

setComponent(
  params,
  component,
  initial_value,
  dynamics_fun,
  encounter_fun,
  mort_fun,
  component_params,
  colour = "grey",
  linetype = "solid",
  definition,
  rate_fun,
  integration_order,
  convergence_fun,
  role,
  stationary,
  equation_rates_fun,
  tuning,
  transformations,
  biomass_fun,
  biomass_filters,
  prescribed_mask_fun,
  autonomous
)

removeComponent(params, component)

getComponent(params, component)

Arguments

params

A MizerParams object

component

Name of the component of interest. If missing, a list of all components will be returned.

initial_value

Initial value of the component. Required for a new component; retained when omitted for an existing component. Must not be NULL; use removeComponent() to remove a component.

dynamics_fun

Name of function to calculate value at the next time step. Required unless rate_fun is supplied.

encounter_fun

Name of function to calculate contribution to encounter rate. Optional.

mort_fun

Name of function to calculate contribution to the mortality rate. Optional.

component_params

Object holding the parameters needed by the component functions. This could for example be a named list of parameters. Optional.

colour

Line colour to use for the component in plots. Defaults to "grey".

linetype

Line type to use for the component in plots. Defaults to "solid".

definition

A named list specifying the component's callbacks and plotting styles. Supplying a list replaces its previous definition before explicitly supplied arguments are applied. State and component parameters are supplied separately. Updating only state or component parameters does not re-adopt capabilities after a global provider change; supply the relevant capability explicitly.

rate_fun

Name of function returning the component's derivative. Required unless dynamics_fun is supplied.

integration_order

Optional positive integer declaring the order of a custom dynamics_fun. NULL removes the declaration.

convergence_fun

Name of a convergence-measurement callback, or NULL to remove it. A dynamic component without this support makes a whole-model assessment incomplete.

role

Either "dynamic" (the default) or "prescribed".

stationary

Explicit TRUE/FALSE stationary-tuning declaration.

equation_rates_fun

Callback exposing effective equation quantities.

tuning

Named strategies and their default, or NULL to remove support.

transformations

Named transformation declarations. Update hooks may modify this component's initial state and parameters; additional paths must be explicit. Use action = 'none' for supported no-action operations.

biomass_fun

Named biomass measurement callback, or NULL to remove measurement support. This is independent of convergence and dynamics.

biomass_filters

Character vector of explicitly supported filters: min_w, max_w, min_l, max_l and use_cutoff. Defaults to none.

prescribed_mask_fun

Named structural input-mask callback, or NULL. For a dynamic numeric component, return logical values with exactly its state dimensions and names; TRUE marks prescribed inputs. The callback receives params and optional component/owner, without time or state.

autonomous

TRUE for equations and contributions without explicit time dependence, FALSE for forced providers, or NULL for undeclared support. This declaration is independent of stationary tuning and convergence.

Value

The updated MizerParams object

For getComponent: A list with the entries initial_value, dynamics_fun, rate_fun, encounter_fun, mort_fun, component_params, convergence_fun, role, and definition for the requested component. If the requested component does not exist, NULL is returned. If no component argument is given, then a list of lists for all components is returned.

Details

The component can be a number, a vector, an array, a list, or any other data structure you like.

A new component needs an initial_value, supplied separately from its definition. Supply at least one of dynamics_fun and rate_fun, directly or through definition. For an existing component, omitted arguments retain their existing values. Explicit NULL removes an optional callback, provided at least one of the two dynamics capabilities remains. Remove a component with removeComponent().

A definition is a reusable named list containing dynamics_fun, rate_fun, encounter_fun, mort_fun, colour, linetype and/or integration_order, convergence_fun, role, stationary, equation_rates_fun and/or tuning. Explicit arguments override its entries. Supplying a definition replaces the component's previous definition: omitted optional callbacks are removed and omitted styles default to "grey" and "solid". Without definition, explicitly supplied arguments patch the existing definition instead. Initial state and component_params belong to the component instance and are retained when omitted, including when its definition is replaced.

The assembled definition is stored in the model. Subsequent changes to the list used as definition do not change that model; call setComponent() again to apply an update. Callback function names are stored, rather than their implementations, so the functions still need to be available when the model is used.

Equations and custom steps

A rate_fun returns the component's derivative, with the numeric shape and names of its state preserved. It receives params, n, n_pp, n_other, rates, t, component and .... Mizer applies Euler under first-order projection and Heun under the second-order methods. This is explicit integration, including when the fish use TR-BDF2.

A dynamics_fun returns the new state and owns the integration. It is the appropriate capability for stiff or non-numeric states. When both callbacks are supplied, the custom step performs projection and the derivative remains available for diagnostics. Callback names may be unqualified or use package::exported_function.

Custom steps may accept predicted_state and endpoint_rates. During a second-order corrector these contain the predicted endpoint state (a list with n, n_pp, n_other and t) and its rate list. They are NULL when no prediction is available. The ordinary state arguments still describe the start of the step. Prediction data do not by themselves establish the accuracy or stability of the custom integration.

integration_order declares the order of a custom step; omission means unknown, not an assumed second order. Replacing dynamics_fun clears an inherited order unless an order is explicitly supplied with the replacement. Mizer chooses the integrator for equations-only components, so they must not declare a custom integration order.

Steady-state assessment

A convergence_fun returns a data frame with measure, value, tolerance and units columns. It receives the model, state, complete rate list, time, derivative when available and component name. Accept ... for unused arguments. Mizer compares absolute measured values to their tolerances; the callback does not return its own pass/fail verdict.

Components are dynamic by default, including legacy components using constant_other. Declare role = "prescribed" explicitly when the entire component is a prescribed input. Temporarily holding a dynamic component fixed during analysis requires conditional assessment scope. Replacing a dynamics callback removes its inherited convergence callback and resets an inherited prescribed role to dynamic unless those declarations are explicitly supplied again with the replacement.
